sections.content:
Population change in Wokingham in 2032

The population in Wokingham is projected to increase from 181,383 people in 2022 to 203,488 people in 2032.

The biggest factor in this population change is net internal migration, which will increase the population by 11,353 people.

This will also be the biggest factor in population change in most areas in England.

sections.title: Contributors to population change in Wokingham
sections.subtitle: How the population is projected to change, by cause
sections.source: Subnational population projections for England from Office for National Statistics – Migration category variant
sections.note: The components of change do not always sum exactly to the total population change in an area. This is primarily due to the effect of constraining the final projections to the National Population Projections for England.

sections.content:
Population change is projected by looking at births and deaths (natural change) and people moving in and out of areas. In Wokingham, our projections show that between 2022 and 2032:

  • More births than deaths mean that the population is projected to increase by 3,475, with 17,853 births and 14,378 deaths in Wokingham between 2022 and 2032. This means natural change would increase the population in Wokingham by 1.9%, compared with an increase of 0.2% in England.
  • Net internal migration (people moving to and from other local authorities in England) is projected to increase the population by 11,353, with 135,003 people moving to the area and 123,650 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would increase the population in Wokingham by 6.3%.
  • Net cross-border migration (between UK nations) is projected to reduce the population by 1,377, with 4,145 people moving to the area and 5,521 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would decrease the population in Wokingham by 0.8%.
  • Net international migration is projected to increase the population by 8,768, with 20,537 people moving to the area and 11,769 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would increase the population in Wokingham by 4.8%, compared with an increase of 6.5% in England.

sections.content:
Age profile in Wokingham in 2032

The median age in Wokingham is projected to rise from 41 years in 2022 to 42 years in 2032.

In England, the median age is projected to be 41 years in 2032.

In 2032, 18% of the population in Wokingham are projected to be aged 65 years or over, up from 16% in 2022.

sections.title: The 0 to 9 age group are set to see the largest change in Wokingham between 2022 and 2032
sections.subtitle: Percentages of population by 10 year age bands, 2022 and 2032
sections.source: Subnational population projections for England from Office for National Statistics – Migration category variant

sections.content:
Between 2022 and 2032, the share of the working age population (people aged 16 years to State Pension age) in Wokingham is projected to stay the same, at around 64%.

The old age dependency ratio (the number of people of State Pension age for every 1,000 people of working age) is projected to stay around the same, at 258 in 2032 compared with 260 in 2022.

This is below average for England in 2032 (287 per 1,000). Nationally, a high old age dependency ratio means more older people are financially reliant on the working age population to pay for pensions.

How will the number of young people change in Wokingham?

In 2032, 22% of people are projected to be aged 18 years and under, down from 25% in 2022.

This is above average for England in 2032 (20%).

Looking at the youngest age groups in Wokingham between 2022 and 2032, we can see the share of:

  • Infants (aged 0 to 4 years) will stay around the same, at 5%
  • Primary school age children (aged 5 to 11 years) will fall from 10% to 8%
  • Secondary school age children and sixth-form age (aged 12 to 18 years) will stay around the same, at 8%
